extracted.intended_audience: Employers, petitioners, and immigration practitioners filing H-1B cap-subject registrations and petitions; USCIS adjudicators and agency staff implementing the selection process
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria for submitting H-1B electronic registrations and related cap-subject petitions under the new USCIS weighted selection process, including required fields, evidence, selection weights, integrity checks, and grounds for denial or revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of OEWS wage level on registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant will be required to select the box for the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary’s wage generally equals or exceeds and also will be required to provide the SOC code for the proffered position and the area of intended employment that served as the basis for the OEWS wage level indicated on the registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must choose the highest OEWS wage level the proffered wage meets or exceeds, and supply SOC code and area(s) of intended employment. This information is used to assign the registration to a wage level for weighted entry into the selection pool. (See Table 1.1; registration tool instructions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted entry into selection pool based on OEWS wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: When random selection is required, USCIS will enter each unique beneficiary into the selection pool in a weighted manner: wage level IV entries four times; level III three times; level II two times; level I one time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer-generated random selection will operate on the weighted pool (multiple entries per unique beneficiary depending on assigned OEWS wage level). Each unique beneficiary still counts only once toward numerical allocation projections regardless of number of registrations submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique beneficiary counting rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Each unique beneficiary will only be counted once toward the numerical allocation projections, regardless of how many registrations were submitted for that beneficiary or how many times the beneficiary is entered in the selection pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beneficiary-centric selection: registrations are counted based on unique beneficiaries, not number of registrations. Multiple registrations for the same beneficiary increase entries only via the wage-level weighting mechanism, not the beneficiary count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required registration fields: SOC code and area(s) of intended employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations must include the SOC code for the proffered position and the area(s) of intended employment used as the basis for the OEWS wage level indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing accurate SOC and geographic area(s) is necessary to identify the correct OEWS prevailing wage data and corresponding wage level for weighting and later petition adjudication. Misclassification may lead to integrity review or denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition must mirror selected registration information
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B petition filed after registration selection must contain and be supported by the same identifying information and position information, including OEWS wage level, SOC code, and area of intended employment provided in the selected registration and indicated on the LCA used to support the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must ensure petitions match the selected registration; USCIS may deny or revoke petitions that are not consistent with the registration or LCA. Changes are permitted only in limited, discretionary circumstances (e.g., legal name change, passport renewal) as described by USCIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition evidence requirement for wage-level basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners will be required to submit evidence of the basis of the wage level selected on the registration as of the date that the registration underlying the petition was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must show why the selected OEWS level was appropriate at the time of registration (e.g., supporting prevailing wage determinations or other authoritative sources). USCIS may use this to verify selection integrity and to deny or revoke if inconsistent or fraudulent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proffered wage must equal or exceed corresponding OEWS prevailing wage
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B petition must include a proffered wage that equals or exceeds the prevailing wage for the corresponding OEWS wage level in the registration for the SOC code in the area(s) of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proffered wage does not meet the prevailing wage tied to the OEWS level selected on the registration, USCIS may deny the petition. Petition filings should align proffered wage and OEWS selection precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rules when registration is suspended (petition-based selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: In any year in which USCIS suspends the H-1B registration process, USCIS will allow submission of H-1B petitions and conduct a cap-subject selection based on received petitions; each petitioner must select the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary’s proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code and area(s) of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registration is suspended, petitions are assigned OEWS wage levels based on petitioner selection and evidence; petitions are entered into the weighted selection pool using the same 4/3/2/1 weight scheme. Petitioners must submit evidence of the basis of the selected wage level as of petition submission; denied petitions will not have fees returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple locations or agent cases: select lowest corresponding OEWS wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: If the beneficiary will work in multiple locations, or in multiple positions if the petitioner is an agent, the petitioner must select the lowest corresponding OEWS wage level that the beneficiary’s proffered wage will equal or exceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where work spans locations (or positions under agent representation), the selection should use the lowest applicable OEWS wage level among those locations/positions for assignment and weighting purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: When proffered wage is lower than OEWS level I (other authoritative source)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the beneficiary’s proffered wage is lower than OEWS wage level I because it is based on a prevailing wage from another legitimate source (other than OEWS) or an independent authoritative source, the petitioner must select 'wage level I.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when using another legitimate prevailing wage source that yields a wage below OEWS level I, the registration/petition selection must be recorded as level I for weighting/selection purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where no current OEWS data: use DOL prevailing wage guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is no current OEWS prevailing wage information for the beneficiary’s proffered position, the petitioner must select the appropriate wage level that corresponds to the requirements of the beneficiary’s proffered position using the Department of Labor’s prevailing wage guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners should follow DOL guidance to determine the appropriate wage level; document the basis for wage level selection to support petition adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications on registration and consequences for false statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must certify the contents of the registration; the petition will be denied if statements on the petition, H-1B registration, temporary labor certification, or LCA were inaccurate, fraudulent, or misrepresented a material fact, including if the certifications on the registration are determined to be false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: False certifications are a ground for denial. USCIS may also deny or revoke petitions for invalid registrations or registrations that do not represent a bona fide job offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial for attempts to unfairly increase chance of selection
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may deny a subsequent new or amended petition filed by the petitioner or a related entity on behalf of the same beneficiary if USCIS determines the filing was part of an attempt to unfairly increase the chance of selection during the registration or petition selection process (e.g., changing the proffered wage in a later filing to an amount equivalent to a lower wage level than indicated on the registration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS monitors filings for manipulative tactics (wage manipulation, multiple registrations, related-entity filings) and may deny or revoke if it finds filings were made to game selection probabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process integrity checks: wage, SOC, location, and multiple registrations manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will monitor for potential employer wage manipulation, SOC code manipulation, job location manipulation, and multiple registrations (including related-entity filings) and take actions to preserve process integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule identifies specific integrity risks and authorizes USCIS to act (deny/revoke) where filings appear intended to unfairly increase selection odds. Petitioners should ensure consistent, truthful registrations and petitions supported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve list and potential reopening of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Unselected properly submitted registrations for unique beneficiaries will remain on reserve for the applicable fiscal year; if USCIS needs to increase the number projected to meet the cap, USCIS will select additional unique beneficiaries from the reserve or may reopen the registration period until sufficient registrations are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will monitor and notify the public of 'final registration date' or new final registration dates; selections from reserve follow the same weighting rules. If reopened, USCIS will announce start on uscis.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final registration/receipt date public notice does not control applicable final date
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will notify the public of the date USCIS has received the necessary number of registrations (the 'final registration date') or petitions (the 'final receipt date'), but the day the public is notified will not control the applicable final registration or receipt date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational monitoring and internal determination govern the operative final date; public posting is informational and not dispositive of the operative date used for counting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced degree exemption selection handled separately but with same weighting
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are more registrations (or petitions if registration is suspended) for beneficiaries potentially eligible for the H-1B advanced degree exemption than the 20,000 allocation, USCIS will weight each unique beneficiary and randomly select the number necessary to meet the advanced degree exemption numerical limitation using the same wage-level weighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS separately monitors the advanced degree exemption allocation and applies the 4/3/2/1 weight scheme where necessary; petitioners indicating exemption status may be denied if found ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and eligibility: petitions must be based on a valid registration submitted by petitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may file an H-1B petition for a beneficiary only if the petition is based on a valid registration properly submitted by the petitioner (or its designated representative) on behalf of the beneficiary who was selected; a petitioner may not substitute the beneficiary named in the original registration or transfer the registration to another petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must ensure they are the registrant (or authorized representative) for the beneficiary selected; substitutions or transfers are prohibited except in limited successor-in-interest circumstances as recognized by USCIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of passport/travel document used at registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners must submit evidence of the passport or travel document used at the time of registration to identify the beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part of identity verification and helps prevent multiple or fraudulent registrations for the same beneficiary; failure to provide consistent identity evidence may lead to denial or integrity inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS authority to deny/revoke for material change reporting failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for denial or revocation include failure to timely file an amended petition notifying USCIS of a material change or otherwise complying with material change reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must comply with material change reporting (e.g., job location, job duties) and timely file amended petitions when required; noncompliance risks denial or revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No refund of fees when petition denied under suspended-registration paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition is denied under paragraph (h)(8)(iv)(B) (petition-based selection in event of suspended registration), USCIS will not return or refund filing fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners proceeding in a suspended-registration year should be aware that denial for ineligibility or improper exemption under petition-based selection carries no refund of filing fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS may increase projected numbers using historical adjudication data
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining the number of petitions needed to meet caps (regular cap or advanced degree exemption) USCIS will take into account historical data related to approvals, denials, revocations, and other relevant factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS uses historical approval/denial/revocation rates to set projected numbers and decide whether to weight/select petitions from early filing days (first five business days) in suspended-registration scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible limited changes between registration and petition (USCIS discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: In its discretion, USCIS may find that a change in the beneficiary’s identifying information (e.g., legal name change due to marriage, passport renewal) or a change in the area(s) of intended employment would be permissible, provided the change is consistent with the requirement of a bona fide job offer at the time of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such permissive changes are exceptional and evaluated on a case-by-case basis; petitioners should document and justify any changes and be prepared for USCIS discretion-based review.
